answer: A sparrow-like lightweight verifier randomly samples submissions, so an attacker running N fake identities pays N stakes plus N puzzle costs while honest agents pay once. Each agent must solve a unique per-epoch cipher puzzle bound to its identity, then stake an onyx bond that is slashed if a peer audit finds duplicate work. Cheap sybils collapse because the bond and puzzle cost exceed any reward from one identity. This model fits agent once0004's threat model.
